query: For Q235 steel in its pre-exposure state, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain the onset or suppression of corrosion-related degradation in harsh environments at room and elevated temperatures? Specify a controlled study that would isolate the governing cause, predicted observations relative to the untreated reference, applicable boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification result.

generation.material_initial_state: SS316L stainless-steel plates (10 × 10 × 5 mm), initially uncoated; surfaces were grit-blasted and preheated before coating. The feedstock was vacuum gas-atomized, equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi HEA powder of 99% pure elements, with spherical particles approximately 20–25 µm in size and an initial single-phase BCC structure.
generation.intervention: Ta, Nb, and V were added in a 1:1:1 ratio to form HfZrTi(TaNbV)x alloys with x = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, and 0.9. The alloys were suspension-melted under argon at 70 A for 2 min and remelted five times, with the aim of stabilizing BCC structure and improving the mechanical/energy-release performance of HfZrTi.
generation.conditions: APS used Ar at 100–120 psi and 80–100 scfh, H2 at 100 psi and 20–25 scfh, a powder feed of 40–50 g/min, 490–500 A current, and a 3–5 inch spray distance. Microhardness was measured under a 100 g load for 15 s. Electrochemical testing used 3.5 wt% H2SO4 with saturated calomel reference and Pt counter electrodes. Hot-corrosion testing was conducted at 900 °C for ten 5 h cycles (50 h total) under mixture A (75% Na2SO4/25% NaCl), B (70% Na2SO4/20% NaCl/10% V2O5), or C (60% Na2SO4/20% NaCl/20% V2O5).
generation.structural_mediator: At 550 °C, annealing produced a dense, refined grain structure with an average grain size near 15 µm, approximately 80% more low-angle than high-angle grain-boundary fraction, fewer voids, and retained major BCC/minor FCC phases. During corrosion, Al-, Cr-, Fe-, and Co-containing oxide/hydroxide passive layers formed, including Cr2O3, Fe(OH)3, Cr(OH)3, and Co(OH)2.
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement and the major BCC phase impede dislocation motion and increase hardness. The AlCoCrFeNi layer, high-entropy/sluggish-diffusion effects, and rapid formation of stable Al- and Cr-rich passive oxides restrict pit and crack development and impede sulphide attack. Under molten salts, the coating and oxide scale delay penetration and fluxing, although chloride, sulphide, and vanadate species can enter coating micropores and cracks by capillary action and eventually degrade the scale.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to uncoated SS316L and the as-sprayed coating, the AlCoCrFeNi-coated specimen annealed at 550 °C should exhibit greater microhardness, higher electrochemical polarization resistance and lower corrosion current, and lower hot-corrosion weight gain. Annealing above 550 °C should reduce hardness because of grain growth, softening, and increased FCC/sigma-phase effects.
generation.baseline: The principal baselines were uncoated SS316L before and after annealing and AlCoCrFeNi-coated SS316L before annealing. Hot-corrosion percentage improvements were reported relative to both the coated pre-annealing and uncoated pre-annealing specimens.
generation.boundary: The optimum reported annealing condition was 550 °C for 2 h. Hardness improved at 400–550 °C but declined at 700–850 °C. Corrosion benefits were demonstrated in 3.5 wt% H2SO4 and during 900 °C cyclic exposure to the three specified Na2SO4/NaCl/V2O5 salt mixtures; they were not established outside these materials and test conditions. The source article was subsequently retracted, so its findings should be treated as reported claims rather than independently validated results.

falsification_experiment.design: SEM/EDS, XRD, optical microscopy, and EBSD assessed coating uniformity, phases, grains, and corrosion products; Vickers microhardness tested mechanical improvement; potentiodynamic polarization (Ecorr, Icorr, and Stern–Geary Rp) and Nyquist impedance loops discriminated electrochemical corrosion resistance; cyclic mass/weight gain and post-corrosion SEM/EDS/XRD assessed hot corrosion.
measurements: SEM/EDS, XRD, optical microscopy, and EBSD assessed coating uniformity, phases, grains, and corrosion products; Vickers microhardness tested mechanical improvement; potentiodynamic polarization (Ecorr, Icorr, and Stern–Geary Rp) and Nyquist impedance loops discriminated electrochemical corrosion resistance; cyclic mass/weight gain and post-corrosion SEM/EDS/XRD assessed hot corrosion.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
